title: GPU Fleet Idle Intervals and Streaming Updates
prompt:
GPU tasks are tuples `(start, end, node_id)`, where start and end are integer timestamps with `start < end`. Each task occupies the half-open interval `[start, end)`. Tasks may arrive out of order or overlap, including on different nodes.

For this exercise, the fleet is idle only when no task is running on any node. `node_id` identifies the task's node but does not partition the idle-time query.

### Part 1 — Batch idle intervals

Implement `idle_intervals(tasks, query_start, query_end)`. Return the sorted, maximal half-open intervals within `[query_start, query_end)` during which the fleet is idle. `query_start < query_end`. Tasks outside the query window have no effect. Do not modify the input.

### Part 2 — Streaming busy intervals

Implement `BusyTimeline.add(start, end, node_id)` and `BusyTimeline.get_idle(query_start, query_end)`. Each add records another task. Keep a merged representation of busy intervals so repeated queries do not sort the full task history. Adjacent busy intervals may be merged. Explain update and query costs in terms of the number of merged intervals.
